title: Comes the Dawning Light
subtitle: Get up. The bloody night is over.

trails.title: Third-Rate Novel
trails.description: Not everyone's life makes a good story. Most of us live inside third-rate novels.

content.text:
Today's tale doesn't start with "once upon a time." It begins in "a quiet, ordinary village." In that village lived an equally ordinary little girl whose father was a vampire. But unlike him, she didn't live apart from humans. She felt a natural fondness toward both humans and arcanists. Perhaps because she was a hybrid—an "impure" half-vampire? In any case, for a long while, the girl lived peacefully with her parents.

Until a shell fell.

Yes, war. Again.

War brings death, and death spreads. Her family didn't escape it; one by one, they died. Only she and her uncle survived, wandering endlessly. But shells don't discriminate. Human, arcanist, vampire, or half-breed—none are spared. The girl was wounded. How badly? No one knows. Severe enough that she nearly died. Her uncle wanted to save her—his only remaining family. Even if it meant making a deal with the devil, he would.

He carried her to an old castle. Its mistress, as all stories go, was powerful and mysterious. She healed the dying hybrid girl. The price—if it could even be called that—was an overactive regenerative power that let her recover from any wound with ease.

Since then, the girl's body has always been wrapped in bandages.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Uncle Pyrrhos, how much farther do we need to go? I'm feeling a little dizzy.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: Not long now. The border's just on the other side of the mountain. We'll be there soon.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: Then we'll cross the Lech to Ms. Valentina's castle.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: And she'll cure you. She'll make things right.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: But how do you know she'll help?

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: I just know, Aima. A vampire always stands by her people. It's in our blood.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: In our blood.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: You'll do well to remember that, Aima.

items.speaker: Pyrrhos
items.text: There is no bond stronger than blood.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Uncle ...
Aima gently sets the wooden matryoshka down.
Its painted smile is unchanged, as if it still remembers the winds along the Danube, the swaying of the train, the murmurs and laughter of her journey.
Now its journey has come to an end.
It should return to where it belongs, a world without walls, without exile.
Perhaps there it will find its answer.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Goodbye.
Warehouse, Nika Checkpoint

items.speaker: Infected Soldier
items.text: Ooogh ... Argh ...
Their leader gone, the monsters prowl restlessly, their roars ripping through the silent snowbound night.
Inside the warehouse, the survivors gather to plan their next move.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Signal's back. I've contacted the Foundation; they're sending reinforcements immediately.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But by the looks of it, the Infected will get to us before the backup arrives.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: It seems Pyrrhos's death hasn't had any effect on them. They're still coming.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Perhaps, if anything, they seem more dangerous.
Semmelweis holds a glance on the shuddering doors of the warehouse, letting out an audible sigh.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: After this, mark my words, this is the last time I take on a mission with vampires.
Watching the situation unfold, Yakov looks down at the weapon in his hands, frowning.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: We're running out of bullets. What do we do?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: We have to take them down. All at once.

items.speaker: Yakov
items.text: All at once? How?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Draw them into a room, and leave the rest to those.
She points toward a number of heavy crates bearing an ominous marking: "flammable."

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I noticed them when we entered, too. Explosives, I presume?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Yes. Pyrrhos mentioned having seized them from a militia camp.

items.speaker: Arbuthnot
items.text: Sounds like a plan. But how do we draw 'em close enough?

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: This isn't a plan; this is madness! Do you seriously believe they'll simply saunter into a building as if it were some kind of concert?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Concert? That's it! We'll play music! Lucky for us, I always carry my kaval with me.
Her ruby eyes sparkle with sudden inspiration as she lifts her flute.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: In the old stories, when the Infected go loopy like this, they're easily attracted to loud noises.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: And my kaval—well, let's just say, if you've got ears, you'll hear it.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: That matches with documentation I've read in the Foundation archives—a feasible solution.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But that would make you the bait. Are you certain you can do it?
Rubuska grips her flute with determination.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Reyhan
items.text: We can't; she's just a child.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Don't go, Rubuska. We nearly lost you once already.
She squeezes her doll.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Don't worry. I can handle it. I run fast. Those Infected won't get close. Besides ...

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Me and my kaval can control shadows. I'll make a whole bunch of them as a distraction.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: See, tell me, who else could pull that off?
One by one, the others shake their heads. Worry and refusal are written across every face, save one.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You're not afraid?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'd be lying if I said no.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: But I'm Rubuska, the all-powerful, the deathless! And you're all counting on me!
Corvus nods, offering her a knowing smile.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Then go. I believe in you, "old pal."

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: See you when this is all over!
She straightens her back and salutes clumsily. Corvus pretends not to see, merely turning away and waving to the others.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: The rest of you, come with me. Time to set the trap.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: There is no room for failure.
Border Checkpoint
Snow still falls.

items.speaker: Infected Soldier
items.text: Ooh ... Argh ...
Infected trudge through the whipping snow, moving step by heavy step.
The girl stands alone, her only companion the wooden flute in her hands.

items.speaker: Infected Soldier
items.text: Arrah ...
Faces rise from the darkness, pale skin clinging to bone, veins etched across them like dry riverbeds.
And in them, she sees another face.
She steps back once, then forward twice.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Mама, forgive me.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: But I'm not running anymore.
The great Rubuska takes a deep breath. Lips meet the waiting flute.
It starts with a few clumsy notes, followed by a jumble of uneven chords. But the chords soon weave together, and the melody resonates up through the biting cold.

items.speaker: Infected Passenger
items.text: Oooh ... Arraagh ...
It is a soft, lonesome tune, one that once carried her through battlefields that had gone quiet, graveyards, and mountains.
Through long years, she was the melody's only listener.
Back then, all she saw was silence stretching to the horizon and futures unseen.
So she recited tale after tale of vampires.

items.speaker: "Dracula the Vampire"
items.text: Before you stands the forefather of young Rubuska—Dracula the Impaler!

items.speaker: "Arnold the Vampire"
items.text: And I, her noble grandfather, the glorious First Duke of Arges!

items.speaker: "Savonovic the Vampire"
items.text: And I ...
That lineage, growing ever more tangled, became her closest companion on the road.
When she comes to, she realizes just how far she has wandered.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Мама!

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: You've come so far, my Buska.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yes, I have.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I crossed the Rila Mountains, waded through-through the Struma River, and traveled along the Danube.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Oh, I even rode a train!

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: You sound happy, my dear girl.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Happy?

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Those sights you've seen, your new friends, the train. I can feel your joy.
In the fading flute's descent, the last note melts into the sunlight.
She tilts her face upward, as if catching the April wind once more.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yes, I am happy.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Happier than I've been in a long time, Mама.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: She's done it. The Infected are swarming together.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Explosives are in place. On my mark.
Corvus waves toward Rubuska.
She instantly understands, slipping out from the shadows until she is free of the Infected's encirclement.
All is ready. The conductress narrows her gaze and gives the final order.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Three, two, one.
Border Checkpoint

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Please form a line and await registration.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: The train will leave at dawn, so please make good use of your time.
Order is at last restored.
The conductress remains behind, watching the snowy way station and the wreckage left by the blast. Blood, organs, and fragments carpet the snow, like scarlet flowers blooming in an instant.
Pyrrhos's corpse is brought forth. Laid at the center of the bloom, his hollow eyes stare into the void.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: This chill in the air ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: The last time I felt a cold like this was in Strandzha. I thought it would be the end of me.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: We were hiding out in the mountains. Every gust of wind felt like icy teeth biting into us.
Snowflakes land in her palm. Soon they will melt away like breath into the cold air.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: *sigh* Aima will continue to work on the "Danube Dawn."

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Who would ever suspect a gentle girl like her of being a vampire? She'll be able to live a quiet life.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: She'll need blood from time to time, and I will provide it.
She mutters to herself, then frowns, glancing to the side.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I see you over there. Come out.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Eyes as sharp as ever, I see. Nothing escapes you.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Do I know you?

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Do you know me? *mocking chuckle* We were partners.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: That is, until you were lost to us in that accident.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I think you have me confused, madam.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Heh ...
She sighs deeply.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Indeed. How unfortunate that the similarities only go skin deep.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Still, who's to say it wasn't a cruel twist of fate that I boarded your train? Because ...

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: In a way, we both lost someone today.
She takes the torch from the conductress's hand, lights it, and casts it on the scattered flesh before them.
The flames rise with a low and crisp murmur.
The two stand together speechless for a time, until the first light of dawn spills across the ground.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Dawn at last. It's been a long night.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Time to go.
She turns toward the train, still halted, waiting like a slumbering iron giant.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: The "Danube Dawn" is ready to set off once again.
